chapter.title: Water — The Essence of Life
chapter.tagline: Discovering states of matter, the water cycle, soil percolation, and river systems
chapter.overview: Afreen and Jyoti watch monsoon raindrops on their window pane. Through hands-on experiments with ice condensation, evaporation in sunlight, and soil percolation, students unpack the water cycle, trace India's major river networks, and understand wetland conservation.

sections.title: Rain at the Window: Observing Water Everywhere
sections.subtitle: Water as the foundational substance supporting all Earth ecosystems

storyNarrative.dialogue: Listen to the raindrops drumming on the tin roof! Where did all this sky water come from, and where does it go after it puddles on the ground?

concept.heading: Ubiquitous Presence of Water
concept.keyRule: Water covers over 70% of Earth's surface and is essential for every biological function and ecosystem.

blocks.title: Interactive Lab: Global Blue Planet 3D Water & Land Ratio Explorer

content.interactiveTitle: Global Blue Planet 3D Water & Land Ratio Explorer
content.pedagogicalObjective: Understand that water covers over 70% of Earth's surface and is essential for all living organisms.
content.explanation: Afreen and Jyoti watch raindrops on their window and wonder how much of Earth is covered by water. Students rotate a 3D Earth globe, toggle ocean and land layers, and discover that over 71% of Earth's surface is blue water.
content.simpleExplanation: Spin planet Earth in 3D to see why our home is called the Blue Planet, covered in 71% shimmering oceans!
content.stemExplanation: Planetary hydrology and geosphere surface area distribution (361 million km² water vs 149 million km² land).

questions.prompt: Approximately what percentage of the Earth's surface is covered by water?
questions.hint: Earth is known as the Blue Planet because over seven-tenths is water.

sections.title: States of Matter & The Condensation Mystery
sections.subtitle: Transitioning between solid ice, liquid water, and gaseous vapour

storyNarrative.dialogue: Afreen, look! When we put ice cubes in a dry steel glass, water droplets appeared on the outside! The glass isn't leaking—where did the water come from?

concept.heading: Condensation of Atmospheric Water Vapour
concept.keyRule: Invisible water vapour in the warm surrounding air cools upon touching the cold glass and condenses into liquid droplets.

blocks.title: Interactive Lab: Ice Tumbler Condensation & States of Matter Lab

content.interactiveTitle: Ice Tumbler Condensation & States of Matter Lab
content.pedagogicalObjective: Demonstrate that atmospheric water vapour condenses into liquid droplets upon touching cold surfaces.
content.explanation: Afreen places ice cubes inside a dry steel glass. Outside droplets appear. In this simulation, students adjust glass temperature from 30°C down to 0°C, watching invisible surrounding air molecules cool and condense into glittering droplets on the exterior metal surface.
content.simpleExplanation: Put ice in a dry metal glass and watch invisible water vapour in the warm air turn into glistening water beads on the outside!
content.stemExplanation: Phase transition equilibria and dew point thermodynamics: P_vapour >= P_sat(T_surface) triggering surface condensation.

questions.prompt: What process causes droplets to form on the outside of a cold tumbler?
questions.hint: Gas cooling into liquid is condensation.

sections.title: The Complete Water Cycle
sections.subtitle: Solar evaporation, cloud formation, and precipitation

storyNarrative.dialogue: The Sun heats oceans and puddles; water turns to vapour and rises; cool air condenses it into clouds; clouds rain down to feed rivers and seas!

concept.heading: The Global Hydrological Cycle
concept.keyRule: Evaporation ➔ Condensation ➔ Precipitation ➔ Collection (Runoff/Infiltration). A perpetual closed thermodynamic cycle.

content.speaker: Afreen
content.dialogue: The Sun heats oceans and puddles; water turns to vapour and rises; cool air condenses it into clouds; clouds rain down to feed rivers and seas!

content.heading: The Global Hydrological Cycle
content.explanation: Evaporation ➔ Condensation ➔ Precipitation ➔ Collection (Runoff/Infiltration). A perpetual closed thermodynamic cycle.
content.keyRule: Evaporation ➔ Condensation ➔ Precipitation ➔ Collection (Runoff/Infiltration). A perpetual closed thermodynamic cycle.

blocks.title: Interactive Lab: Thermodynamic Global Water Cycle Machine

content.pedagogicalObjective: Trace the continuous closed cycle of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.
content.explanation: Students control the global water cycle. By increasing solar heat, ocean water evaporates into vapour; cooling upper air condenses vapour into fluffy cumulus clouds; saturating clouds precipitates rain and snow over mountains, flowing back to rivers.
content.simpleExplanation: Control the Sun and weather to see how water journeys from the sea to the sky as clouds, rains down on hills, and flows right back home!
content.stemExplanation: Conservation of mass in closed thermodynamic planetary hydrologic systems (Q_solar -> latent heat of vaporization -> adiabatic cooling -> precipitation).

questions.prompt: What energy source drives the global water cycle?
questions.hint: Solar energy evaporates water from oceans and lakes.

sections.title: Soil Water Percolation & Groundwater Recharge
sections.subtitle: How rainwater seeps through permeable soil to recharge aquifers

storyNarrative.dialogue: When we poured water onto garden soil, it soaked deep inside, but on concrete it just flowed away! Soil acts like a giant sponge that fills our underground wells!

concept.heading: Infiltration and Aquifer Recharge
concept.keyRule: Permeable topsoil allows rain to percolate into aquifers. Concreting urban surfaces prevents recharge and causes flash floods.

content.speaker: Jyoti
content.dialogue: When we poured water onto garden soil, it soaked deep inside, but on concrete it just flowed away! Soil acts like a giant sponge that fills our underground wells!

content.heading: Infiltration and Aquifer Recharge
content.explanation: Permeable topsoil allows rain to percolate into aquifers. Concreting urban surfaces prevents recharge and causes flash floods.
content.keyRule: Permeable topsoil allows rain to percolate into aquifers. Concreting urban surfaces prevents recharge and causes flash floods.

blocks.title: Interactive Lab: Soil Infiltration & Aquifer Percolation Tank

content.pedagogicalObjective: Observe how permeable topsoil allows rainwater percolation to recharge underground aquifers, while impermeable surfaces cause runoff.
content.explanation: Jyoti pours water on garden soil and watches it soak in, while on concrete it puddles and runs away. Students pour rain onto 3 soil columns (Garden Loam, Sand, Concrete) to observe percolation rates and well replenishment.
content.simpleExplanation: Pour water through loam soil, sand, and concrete to discover why gardens drink rainwater to fill underground wells, while concrete causes puddles and city floods!
content.stemExplanation: Darcy's Law for porous media fluid flow: Q = -K · A · (dh/dl), hydraulic conductivity and permeability coefficients across soil textures.

questions.prompt: Why is garden soil better than concrete for replenishing groundwater?
options: Soil is permeable and allows water to seep down
questions.correctAnswer: Soil is permeable and allows water to seep down

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look at the river map of India! Ganga, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, Narmada... and around every pond, lotus leaves and frogs thrive!

concept.heading: River Basins as Lifelines
concept.keyRule: Rivers provide freshwater, fertile silt for agriculture, and sustain rich aquatic and wetland ecosystems.

blocks.title: Interactive Lab: Interactive River Basins & Wetland Ecosystem Map

content.interactiveTitle: Interactive River Basins & Wetland Ecosystem Map
content.pedagogicalObjective: Map major river basins of India and understand wetland biodiversity and water conservation.
content.explanation: Afreen studies a physical map of Indian river systems: Ganga, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, Narmada. Students click on river basins to follow their courses and inspect wetland ecosystems supporting lotus leaves, fish, and migratory birds.
content.simpleExplanation: Explore the great rivers of India from mountain snow to ocean waves, and meet the amazing birds and fish living in peaceful wetlands!
content.stemExplanation: Topographical fluvial geomorphology, watershed catchment delineation, and Ramsar wetland ecological conservation indices.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a major river flowing through peninsular India?
questions.hint: Godavari is often called the Dakshin Ganga.
